posts.title: Anna's grandmother's garnets, remade
posts.excerpt: A Victorian brooch nobody wore became a drop pendant and three tassels.
posts.content:
Anna brought in a brooch with eleven garnets, two of them loose, and a broken pin. We kept the best stone for a drop pendant and used the gold from the brooch frame for three small tassels.

It took five weeks. The brooch gold was 15ct, so the new parts are 15ct too, hallmarked in Birmingham with the old mark noted on the certificate.

posts.title: Choosing a sapphire from a tray of rough
posts.excerpt: Why I buy some stones uncut, and what you can tell before they are polished.
posts.content:
Twice a year a cutter in Ratnapura sends me a tray of rough sapphires. Most are grey and cloudy. A few are the colour of the sea off Cromer in February, which is the colour people ask for.

Buying rough is cheaper and I know where the stone came from. It is also slower: cutting adds four weeks to a commission.

posts.title: Why most of my diamonds are old
posts.excerpt: Old cut stones sparkle differently, cost less and are already in the world.
posts.content:
An old European cut diamond has a small table and a tall crown. Under candlelight it looks like a fire. Under a shop spotlight it looks a bit sleepy, which is why the trade underprices them.

I buy them loose from two dealers in Hatton Garden. For most rings they cost 20 to 40 percent less than a new stone of the same size. That is my opinion and I am sticking to it.

posts.title: Sizing a ring for a big knuckle
posts.excerpt: When the knuckle is two sizes bigger than the finger.
posts.content:
If a ring fits the knuckle it spins on the finger. If it fits the finger it will not go over the knuckle. The fix is a slightly squared inside, or two small beads of gold at the bottom of the shank.

Either way, measure the knuckle and the base of the finger and send me both numbers.

posts.title: Workshop open day, Saturday 13 December
posts.excerpt: Come and try the tools. Mince pies, no hard sell.
posts.content:
The workshop is open from 11 to 4 on Saturday 13 December. You can file a bit of silver, look at stones under the microscope and see waxes for rings that are on the bench now.

The stairs are steep and there is no lift, sorry. Brass will be there.
